message:
chore(infection): stop counting #[OA\*] attribute prose as untested code

Infection mutates the concatenation dots in method-level #[OA\*]
arguments, and no test can ever be credited with those lines. 1221 such
mutants held MSI at 50.095% against a floor of 50. Each of the 71
description arguments now carries an ignore comment; the OpenAPI output
is unchanged. Also reorder the session refusal messages so each names
its condition first.
Merge fix/msi-headroom: attribute prose stops counting as untested code

ci(build-image): refuse a release tag that is not on master

Releases are cut from master, but a push trigger cannot filter tags by
branch, so a v1.0.1 cut on a feature branch built and published anyway.
The workflow now checks that the tagged commit is on master before
building.

ci(build-image): register the release with Sentry, not just its name

Events already carry the release name baked into the image, but Sentry
never learned the release itself, so regression detection and suspect
commits had nothing to attach to. The workflow now creates the release
and associates the commits.

feat(kernel): add Option and Result to carry absence and failure in the type

Option (Some, None) and Result (Ok, Err) join the kernel categories with
Rust's methods wherever PHP can express them; the interface docblocks
list what was left out. Nothing calls them yet.

feat(kernel): enforce sealed Option/Result variants and must-use Results in PHPStan

Option and Result are sealed to their two variants, and the
isSome/isNone/isOk/isErr checks narrow to the variant with its type
arguments. New PHPStan rules reject a discarded Result and any other
implementer; each rule has its own test.

chore(coverage): make the gitignore entry match the coverage symlink too

/public/coverage loses its trailing slash so it matches the symlink as
well as a directory.

docs(tasks): specify TASK-044 and TASK-045, what a signer submits at the commit

Design only; nothing is built. TASK-044 records a recipient's field
values at the commit, with filled_fields on both commit routes. ADR-0068
and ADR-0069 are approved as the go-ahead to implement; both stay
Proposed until the work exercises them.

feat(kernel): let a problem extension carry a list of flat records

ADR-0068. A refusal that names several inputs at once, such as a commit
whose field values are wrong in five places, could only answer one field
per round trip or hide a list inside a string. The extension seam now
accepts a list of flat records.

feat(envelope): add the rules a commit's field values are judged by

TASK-044, domain half. Envelope::fieldsShownTo() is the one key set that
both the commit and send() ask about, and the rules define what a
recipient may answer and what counts as a valid answer.

feat(session): carry the recipient's field values into Envelope at the commit

Both commit routes take filled_fields and record them once, inside the
commit's own transaction, through
EnvelopeCommandInterface::recordFieldValues() under the envelope's root
lock. A wrong value is refused with a list of field errors.

feat(envelope): read recorded field values back and refuse a field nobody can answer

TASK-044. FieldView carries the recorded value on both the sender and
the recipient surfaces, and a new RESERVATIONS field type (ADR-0069)
places a recipient's reservations on the page. send() now refuses a data
field assigned to a recipient who fills none, closing BL-60.

docs(task-044): publish the field-values contract and update every record

Adds the FieldValueError schema and its closed code enum to the spec,
the handoffs for the signer and the dashboard, and brings the task, the
ADR indexes and the domain models up to date with what the six earlier
commits built.
Merge feat/field-values-at-commit: TASK-044, field values are recorded at the commit

fix(signature-execution): refuse to seal with a certificate that does not cover the date

DssHttpAdapter checks the seal certificate's validity against the
signing date before any signing call. Outside it, sealing fails with
SealCertificateNotValidException naming the validity and the date,
instead of a retried DSS 500.
Merge origin/develop: the seal refuses a date it does not cover

docs(adr): accept ADR-0068 and ADR-0069 and draft ADR-0070 on declining

ADR-0068 and ADR-0069 are promoted after TASK-044 exercised them.
ADR-0070 is drafted as Proposed: a decline becomes a recipient's outcome
only, EnvelopeStatus::DECLINED, which nothing ever wrote, is retired,
and a voided envelope is sealed as it stands.

docs(adr): re-cut ADR-0070's annulment seal and approve it for TASK-046

The annulment seal draws no mark and names the declining recipient by id
only, void refuses READY_TO_SEAL, and a seal failure behaves like the
completion seal's. The status census is dropped. The record stays
Proposed until TASK-046 exercises it.

refactor(envelope): end an envelope COMPLETED or VOIDED, retire EnvelopeStatus::DECLINED

ADR-0070. Who ended an envelope without agreement is its cause, not a
second status. A void at READY_TO_SEAL is refused as
ENVELOPE_REACHED_AGREEMENT, which also closes a race with the completion
sealer. The annulment seal writes no /Reason, because DSS 6.4's REST
interface refuses it with a 500.

feat(envelope): a decline closes the recipient's leg and a blocking one voids the envelope

ADR-0070 §2.2-2.3, TASK-046. recordRecipientDecline() closes the leg as
DECLINED with the reason and the access method proved, counts it on the
step and records RecipientDeclined. For a blocking recipient the
envelope is voided with the decline as its cause.

fix(db): make every SECURITY DEFINER function search pg_temp last

A new migration puts pg_temp last in the search_path of the 12 definer
functions, so a caller's temporary objects can no longer replace a name
inside them. SchemaConformanceTest fails on any definer function that
does not do so.

feat(session): a recipient may decline on POST /signing/decline; a void is sealed

ADR-0070 §2.4, TASK-046. SigningSession::decline() closes the session as
DECLINED and records SessionDeclined, which crosses into Envelope the
way SessionCompleted does. A voided envelope's document is sealed by an
annulment seal that keeps earlier signatures valid.

feat(session): serve a voided envelope's sealed record to recipients who acted

ADR-0070 §2.6. Recipients who signed or declined read the sealed
annulment of what they did; one who never acted is refused. The envelope
read now publishes void_cause, voided_by_recipient_id and each decline's
reason, and an HTTP test plays a third signer's decline through to the
sealed PDF. Handoffs and records are updated.

docs(adr): measure an external system's capability before approving an ADR's text

ADR-0070 was approved with the annulment stated in the seal's /Reason,
which the PAdES library has and EU DSS 6.4's REST interface refuses.
TASK-046's first step found it and the record was re-cut the same day;
the authoring convention now asks for the measurement first.

docs(task-046): fix docblocks and models that still described decline as unbuilt

Moves the orphaned docblock back onto its
SigningSessionUnavailableException factory, marks decline as built in
the domain model rows, and says the company seal also closes a voided
envelope's chain. Adds a test that a seal on a completed envelope is
refused by status alone.

fix(signature-execution): leave a terminal envelope unsealed by SealDocumentUseCase

A voided envelope's chain admits exactly one seal, and a per-document
seal landing first would take that slot under a foreign execution. The
annulment seal test now asks the live DSS whether both earlier
signatures still validate. ADR-0070 is accepted and the models and
LIVE_SCHEMA catch up.

docs(adr): make every record that called ADR-0070 Proposed say Accepted

The promotion missed TASK-046's Status cell and two rows of the domain-
model README.
Merge develop into feat/recipient-decline: validate the tree develop will receive
Merge feat/recipient-decline: TASK-046, a recipient may decline and the envelope is voided

fix(migrations): rename TASK-046's migration to Version20260925000001

Two branches created Version20260923000001 independently: the pg_temp
hardening on origin/develop and TASK-046's envelope and recipient
columns on the unpushed local develop. Doctrine records a migration by
class name only, so one would have been skipped. The unpushed one is
renamed.

Merge origin/develop into develop: every SECURITY DEFINER function searches pg_temp last

Merges cleanly because TASK-046's migration was renamed first, so each
version is used once.

test(migrations): a migration's class matches its file and its version is a generated time

Two branches hand-picked the same version on one day, and a dev database
that had run one silently skipped the other. A test now refuses a
mismatched class name or a version that is not a generated timestamp;
the docs say to generate migrations instead of numbering them.
Merge chore/generated-migration-versions: a migration's version is its generation time

docs(adr): add ADR-0073 on how an envelope ends, with TASK-048, 049 and 050

ADR-0073 (Proposed) is forced by the Factor5 waybill, where one
consignee's refusal voided the envelope for everyone, and by the gap
between a signer's act and DSS stamping its bytes. TASK-048, 049 and 050
realize it.

feat(envelope): add ADR-0073's ending rules as a pure evaluator with a catalog of flows

EnvelopeEndingEvaluator decides one trigger (a commit, a decline, the
sweep, close-now, a void, a step activation) and is checked against a
catalog of signing flows. It is not wired into the aggregate yet:
nothing here persists, locks or publishes.

feat(evidence-audit): add the audit trail model, its JSON form and chain

Adds the trail's one value (envelope, terminal fact, parties, documents,
facts, checks and limitations, with absence and personal data as
explicit types), the published f5sign.audit-trail/1 JSON form and the
sha256-chain/1 fold over its facts.

feat(envelope): a recipient can be released; the ending vocabulary becomes a contract type

ADR-0073 publishes an envelope's outcome, end cause and each release's
reason and releaser on events and the API, so the four enums the
evaluator decides with move from Domain/Service to Contract/Type,
unchanged.

test(evidence-audit): cover the audit trail model and its published form

Unit tests for the trail value, the chain fold and the JSON form, plus
the shared test doubles and an acceptance test.

feat(envelope): add the schema for admitting acts and ending an envelope

ADR-0073, TASK-048. A migration renames the ending columns and adds the
recipient admission and engagement columns, and the API schema config
follows. This is the first step of the series that admits every act
under the envelope's root lock.

test(evidence-audit): pin the audit trail's chain and golden JSON

The remaining tests of the model: the chain's tamper and ordering
properties and the golden published form, so a change to either fails by
name.

build(docker): pin Typst 0.15.1 by checksum

A build stage downloads the official static binary and verifies its
SHA-256 for amd64 and arm64; an unknown architecture fails the build.
The dev and runtime stages copy the same bytes.

feat(envelope): admit every act under the root lock in the domain

Envelope gains admitCommit and admitDecline, which take the root lock
and re-check the envelope before an act counts, and the ending rules now
drive one lifecycle with an outcome and an end cause. Session,
Notification and SignatureExecution types follow the new vocabulary.

feat(envelope): wire admission and the single seal path through application and adapters

Session commits, delegated commits and declines cross once into
Envelope, an unagreed envelope ends through the one seal path, and the
persistence adapters write the new columns narrowly.

feat(evidence-audit): render the audit trail as PDF/A-3a

Adds the TrailRenderer port, which reports the Typst version and
template hash it uses and returns every failure as a value, and a Typst
adapter with its template and fonts. A trail generated under another
Typst version is refused.

test(envelope): cover admission and the ending rules at the application and HTTP tiers

Envelope application, integration and acceptance tests, with the fakes
they need, for admission under the root lock and the new ending flow.

feat(signature-execution): add a PdfSealer contract port; lock event-log appends by stream

PdfSealer lets another context seal a PDF with the platform seal and
returns every failure as a value. platform.append_event now takes a
shared transaction-level advisory lock on its stream's bucket before its
INSERT; stored rows are unchanged.

test(envelope): cover the ending rules, the event payloads and the notices

Unit tests for the Envelope domain, the foundation and kernel changes,
the notifications and the session acceptance of the new flow.

test(envelope): cover session, sealing and payloads for admission under the root lock

Session and SignatureExecution tests plus the event payload checks that
finish the series: an act admitted before a void still lands inside the
sealed document.

feat(event-log): read one stream of the log, settled, for its tenant

platform.read_settled_stream() is the application's one read of the log.
It returns a stream's rows for the caller's tenant in position order up
to the first boundary fact, after waiting for the stream's open writers.
Refusals come back as rows.

docs(evidence-audit): record the audit trail's design and add the readers it needs

ADR-0072 (Proposed) describes one sealed PDF/A-3a per envelope, rendered
from the settled stream with its JSON input attached. Also adds MarkText
as a contract rule for the visible mark and DocumentArtifactChains, a
read of an envelope's artifact chains.

feat(envelope): keep, promote or discard an ended envelope by whether anyone engaged

ADR-0073 §2.14, TASK-048. Engaged means a recipient who acted, or who
opened or authenticated before the close. Promotion now names the
documents of an envelope that has completed_at set and has someone
engaged.

feat(kernel): add Options::fromNullable and the commit evidence and tenant name readers

Options::fromNullable() returns None for null and Some otherwise.
Session gains CommitEvidenceReader and identity-access gains
TenantNames, the contract reads the audit trail assembles from.

feat(envelope): alarm on a seal pending past two hours; retry chain conflicts to the end

ADR-0073 §2.17. An envelope closed and not yet COMPLETED waits for every
admitted signature, and nothing else would say so if one cannot land, so
app:envelope:report-pending-seals names each one closed too long ago.
The living docs now describe one lifecycle with an outcome and an end
cause.

feat(session): admit at the gate by one rule; record the opening before minting anything

ADR-0073 §2.3, §2.9, §2.14. Every access-gate route asks one question:
the leg is open and the envelope accepts acts, or the recipient already
signed or their role is informational. A closed leg says so, and the
opening is recorded before any credential is minted.

feat(signature-execution): read back the signatures in a PDF

SignatureReadBack returns every signature as DSS's validation reports
it: level, the length of the revision it signs, certificate name and
SHA-256, validation result and timestamps. Each failure is a value.

feat(envelope): migrate every existing row per status and reconcile the rest after deploy

TASK-048 §3.5. The migration adds its columns, maps each row by status,
then adds the checks, and refuses to run over rows it cannot map. A
post-deploy command reconciles what needs the aggregate. The migration
is unpublished, so its SQL is rewritten in place.

test(envelope): race every act against a void and a decline across two processes

A child process takes one act through the production path while the
parent voids or declines, in both orders, and the ending holds. Writers
that can run after send now save narrowly, since save() upserts every
document row and a signing holds those across its DSS calls; a census
keeps them that way.

feat(evidence-audit): let the trail state what a source could not give

A party's act is signed or declined, with a decline's time and reason
kept verbatim outside the personal group. A void states its cause and
reason as statements; no producer records a cause yet, so the cause is
absent.

feat(evidence-audit): make the trail's checks name what it can observe

NO_SESSION_BEFORE_CLAIM replaces NO_CREDENTIAL_BEFORE_CLAIM, since no
fact records a credential, and ASSERTED_DIGESTS_IN_CHAIN replaces
ASSERTED_DIGESTS_MATCHED.

fix(signature-execution): retry a lost chain race for about three hours, then park it

ADR-0073 §2.17. A lost document-chain race was retried without limit,
which would hide a conflict that never resolves. The retry curve now
outlasts the pending-seal alarm and then parks the message. Censuses
check that every gate route asks the gate rule and every act asks
whether the envelope accepts acts.

feat(evidence-audit): assemble the trail from its sources

TrailAssembler makes an envelope's trail from the settled stream, the
envelope, the artifact chains, the commit evidence, the tenant label and
the digests and read-back of each document's final bytes. ADR-0072 and
the domain model describe it.

test(envelope): cover a parked signature; harden the gate's opening write and route docs

A signature admitted before the close but never landing is alarmed three
hours later and sealed in when replayed. The gate's opening write no
longer refuses the gate when its row lock times out. ENVELOPE_BUSY and
LEG_CLOSED are declared on every route that can answer them, and the
envelope model is rewritten as one lifecycle.

test(envelope): old EnvelopeCompleted payloads decode; migration handles parked signatures

A completed event logged before TASK-048 decodes as an agreement and the
new events round-trip. In the unpublished migration, a voided row sealed
around a parked signature admits no act for it. A signature admitted
before a void and landing after it is shown inside the sealed document.

fix(envelope): warn on an unrecorded gate opening; record took-effect acts as landed

The gate proceeds when the opening's row lock times out, which is fail-
open, so the miss is now logged at warning with ids only. The migration
records every admitted act that already took effect as landed, whatever
its mode or role, so only a parked signing waits. Docs read the
reconciliation as done.

docs(task-048): accept ADR-0073, record its amendments in six ADRs and close the task

TASK-048's Status names its branch and the full-regression result, and
its deviations are filled in. Six sibling ADRs carry ADR-0073's
amendments.

test(evidence-audit): cover the trail assembler

Tests for the assembler: each source maps to its part of the trail, and
a missing or unreadable source is stated rather than invented.

feat(task-050): AT_LEAST declines reach the envelope; informational commits are refused

Session no longer refuses a decline in a quorum step; the envelope
judges it by the step's rules. Informational members (viewer, reviewer,
editor) never hold a step, and their commit is refused by name.

feat(evidence-audit): gather the trail's sources through the ports

AuditTrailSources collects an envelope's sources through the contract
ports of the contexts that hold them: the settled stream, the envelope
and its chains, commit evidence, the tenant's name and custody's
digests.

feat(task-049): let a draft hold its sender's chosen life and have send resolve the date

The create route took no life and always used thirty days. A draft now
holds expires_in_days (optional, default 30, 1 to 180) and send()
resolves the date from it. Past its date an envelope admits nothing, and
the sender's writes that prepare an act are refused by name.

feat(evidence-audit): render a trail from the console

app:evidence-audit:render-trail reads an ended envelope's sources under
the tenant's scope, assembles, renders and seals its trail, and writes
the sealed PDF, the plain PDF and the JSON to a directory.

feat(task-050): tell informational members their sealed copy is ready

ADR-0073 §2.15. When an envelope completes with a sealed document,
viewers, reviewers and editors receive a new SEALED_COPY_READY notice
with a link minted in the same reaction.

fix(evidence-audit): correct the trail's contact label and creation time, accept ADR-0072

The label said the contacts a code was sent to were verified, which is
not so when the code was never entered. The creation time now comes from
the creation fact instead of the envelope row, which keeps whole
seconds. ADR-0072 is accepted, realization partial; cspell accepts
"typst".

feat(task-049): the sender extends a sent envelope's date, each extension a recorded fact

POST /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/expiry-extensions takes an RFC 3339
expires_at and answers 200 with the date now in force (ADR-0073 §2.12).
Envelope::extendExpiry() only moves the date forward and may be
repeated.

Merge feat/step-policy: informational members never hold a step; AT_LEAST declines count

Conflicts in the recipient views and the envelope context handler were
resolved by keeping both sides.

fix(evidence-audit): an unreadable DSS body is a failure value; state the annulment seal

A 2xx answer whose body is not JSON, or is cut off, is reported as the
service being unavailable, so PdfSealer and SignatureReadBack keep their
promise to throw nothing. A seal in the trail names its purpose,
completion or annulment, and the published codes are pinned by test.

feat(task-049): expire an envelope at its date, closed by a per-minute sweep

The ending rules now get the envelope's real expires_at. From that date
every act, void and step activation is refused as expired, and a sweep
running each minute ends the envelopes that are due (ADR-0073 §2.12).
The spec names the step predicate the merged aggregate runs.

feat(notification): five notice purposes for an envelope ending without agreement (EN, ES)

One purpose per copy variant of TASK-040: the sender's cancellation with
and without a reason, a participant declined, the time allowed ran out,
and a close by the sender.

feat(notification): tell every invited recipient when an envelope ends without agreement

Notification now consumes EnvelopeVoided alongside Session's subscriber,
which it neither merges with nor assumes ran. The reactor carries the
envelope id, the end cause and the sender's reason, and the notice is
worded by cause.

docs(envelope): the void reason reaches invited recipients; no invitations after the close

VoidEnvelopeRequest::$reason had no #[OA\Property] and read like an
internal note, though the ending notice quotes it verbatim. An
activation, correction or resend handled after the envelope closed now
invites nobody.

Merge feat/step-policy: copy-ready and ending notices classify each other in every match

Both branches added NotificationPurpose cases and copy catalogs; every
conflict kept both sides.

feat(task-049): anchor conservation at the envelope's end; retire EnvelopeStatus::EXPIRED

At COMPLETED the ceiling becomes the later of the provisional one and
completed_at plus the retention months (ADR-0073 §2.16). An expired
envelope is COMPLETED with end_cause EXPIRED. An HTTP test with the
database clock pinned plays the delivery bar, and the life column
carries no database default.

feat(evidence-audit): issue the audit trail when an envelope ends

A reactor on ENVELOPE_COMPLETED and ENVELOPE_VOIDED renders and seals
the trail, records it in evidence_audit.issued_trail and writes the
sealed PDF to a transient custody filed under the envelope, all in one
commit with the custody's first write (ADR-0076).

feat(task-050): let informational members of a never-activated step read the sealed copy

Session refused them with STEP_NOT_ACTIVE even after the envelope
completed. They can now read once it closes. A released member also
loses their session unless the gate still lets them read, by an
asynchronous revoke that mirrors the void path.

docs(task-040): say the recipient is told when an envelope ends without agreement

ADR-0059, ADR-0070 and the Notification model described the ending
notice as missing or void-only. The void reason's contract now says
notices go by email whole, since no ending notice routes to SMS yet. A
displaced test docblock is moved back to its helper.

feat(evidence-audit): let the tenant download the audit trail

GET /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/audit-trail serves the sealed trail as
registro-<envelope id>.pdf with a strong ETag, to any API key of the
tenant. An envelope with no trail for the tenant is a 404. The void
golden now states SENDER_VOIDED.

docs(task-040): correct the Notification model's purpose count to eleven

The sync said "a dozen"; the enum has eleven cases.

feat(evidence-audit): state a decline in the trail; expose the conservation ceiling

A party that declined states it as its act with time and reason, and a
void a decline made names that party in declined_by. A reason appears
only when a sender made it. ConservationCeilings::of() lets another
context read an envelope's ceiling, and LIVE_SCHEMA documents the
evidence_audit schema.

test(task-049): cover the expiry-extension route's isolation; fix its retry documentation

The route had no HTTP negative case for a stranger tenant, a missing
credential or a recipient's credentials. A retry after a lost 200 is
documented as a 409 EXPIRY_NOT_FORWARD, not as idempotent. The domain
model, live schema and task record are updated, and the expiry half of
BL-202 is closed.

feat(task-050): author a step with its completion policy, veto and deadline

POST /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/steps accepts completion (ALL by default, or
AT_LEAST with min_signatures), veto for AT_LEAST only and deadline_hours
of at least 24. send() refuses a policy it cannot judge.

feat(evidence-audit): keep each audit trail as long as its envelope

app:evidence-audit:conserve-trails raises each issued trail's custody to
its envelope's conservation ceiling and records the ceiling and when. It
runs hourly on the custodian's schedule.

docs(adr): record that the audit trail's trigger, route and custodian were exercised

ADR-0072 and its index row record the dev-stack exercise: a trail
issued, served and conserved for a completed, a sender-voided and a
declined envelope, and after a DSS outage and its retry.

fix(evidence-audit): hold one document's bytes at a time; a corrupt trail is unavailable

The trail's sources keep digests instead of bytes and release each
document before reading the next. A stored trail whose bytes fail their
digest is answered with 409 AUDIT_TRAIL_UNAVAILABLE naming the envelope
only. CommitEvidenceReader declares its invalid-subject exception, and
the cost of retrying a voided trail is documented.

docs(evidence-audit): record the trail's open risks and why it renders with Typst

ADR-0072 lists a decline landing after the void, conservation written
once, and an envelope that expires with no trail (BL-312), and explains
why not mPDF, TCPDF or WeasyPrint. The renderer's job-directory limit is
filed as BL-321.
Merge feat/evidence-audit: ADR-0072, each ended envelope gets a sealed audit trail

feat(task-050): let a sender close an envelope whose agreement is secured

Envelope::closeNow() releases every member still open with released_by
SENDER_CLOSED. It runs as a command under the root lock, like the void,
and POST /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/close answers 204 (also on a repeat) or
409 ENVELOPE_AGREEMENT_NOT_SECURED. EnvelopeClosedBySender has frozen
payload bytes.

fix(task-050): judge a step by the veto and deadline it was authored with

Envelope::snapshot() built each step's policy from min_signatures alone,
so an authored veto or deadline was stored and published but never seen
by the ending rules. The signing gate now publishes both what happened
to this participation and how the envelope ended, as two fields.
Merge feat/envelope-expiry: an envelope expires at its sender's date, closed by a sweep
Merge feat/ending-notice: invited recipients are told when an envelope ends
Merge feat/close-now: a sender can close a secured envelope
